title: Introduce RAG mini-orchestrator quickstart with plugin bindings and telemetry
author: Priya Nair
release_notes: Add a compact RAG mini-orchestrator quickstart that demonstrates local plugin bindings, a TypeScript sample orchestrator, devcontainer for reproducible development, and smoke CI for e2e authoring checks.
commit_summaries: init: add mini-orchestrator example and README
feat: plugin binding adapters and lightweight tool API
docs: quickstart guide, devcontainer and troubleshooting notes
ci: add smoke workflow to verify sample on push
fix: address race in local kv-cache mock and update tests
review_comments: Lina Gomez: Nice compact sample — can we make the telemetry probes opt-out by default? Some customers want minimal telemetry in quickstarts.
Author (Priya): Switched probes to opt-out, documented the flag in quickstart.md and added a note about privacy and CI telemetry sampling.
Ethan Wright: The orchestrator example uses an async queue; recommend a small unit test to show deterministic ordering and avoid flaky CI.
Author (Priya): Added a deterministic smoke test and a mockable clock in plugin-adapter to stabilize CI.

description:
Context and motivation: This PR adds a compact RAG "mini-orchestrator" quickstart aimed at engineers who want a minimal, reproducible authoring environment for tool-calling RAG flows. The goal is to provide a small TypeScript orchestrator that demonstrates: local plugin bindings (HTTP and in-process adapters), predictable KV-cache mocking for authoring/eval, an opt-out telemetry probe set for quickstarts, and a smoke CI workflow that verifies the example runs on push.

What changed: added a new quickstart under quickstarts/rag-mini-orchestrator with the following artifacts: a step-by-step quickstart.md, a README with design rationale, an examples/ directory with orchestrator.ts (the coordinator) and plugin-adapter.ts (adapter shim), a devcontainer.json for reproducible local development, and a GitHub Actions smoke workflow that runs a deterministic end-to-end authoring check. Also included: a tiny deterministic unit test harness for the local queue and a short troubleshooting section for common environment issues.

Checklist: 
- [x] TypeScript example orchestrator and plugin adapter included
- [x] Quickstart guide and README with step-by-step run instructions
- [x] Devcontainer for reproducible dev environment
- [x] Opt-out telemetry probes with documentation
- [x] Deterministic smoke CI and unit test to stabilize runs
- [x] Reviewer feedback addressed and docs expanded

Commits (high level):
- init: scaffold quickstart and README
- feat: implement orchestrator core and adapter shim with interface comments
- test: add deterministic queue tests and CI job
- docs: authoring guide, telemetry opt-out and troubleshooting
- ci: smoke workflow that runs in the devcontainer image

Changed areas (high level files):
- quickstarts/rag-mini-orchestrator/README.md — design rationale, adapter contract and mapping to tool-binding spec
- quickstarts/rag-mini-orchestrator/quickstart.md — step-by-step runbook for local authoring and seeding an index
- quickstarts/rag-mini-orchestrator/examples/orchestrator.ts — minimal orchestrator illustrating message loop, streaming to client, and fallback to cached embeddings
- quickstarts/rag-mini-orchestrator/examples/plugin-adapter.ts — two adapter implementations (local in-process stub and HTTP shim) and guidance for authoring your own
- quickstarts/rag-mini-orchestrator/devcontainer.json — reproducible environment with node, yarn and tooling
- ci/workflows/rag-mini-orch-smoke.yml — lightweight smoke e2e check that spins up the devcontainer and runs the sample

Testing and CI: The GitHub Actions workflow executes the sample inside the devcontainer and runs the deterministic smoke test that asserts: example completes within resource limits, deterministic ordering holds for the queue, plugin-adapter returns expected tool outputs, and telemetry opt-out behaves correctly. Initial runs flaked due to a mock clock race; added a mockable clock dependency and a test harness to stabilize results. Final CI status: pass (full matrix: node 18, node 20).

Review conversation (excerpt):
Lina: "Can we ensure telemetry is disabled by default in quickstarts?" 
Priya: "Telemetry is now opt-out; quickstart.md documents the RAG_MINI_ORCH_TELEMETRY=0 flag and acceptable use. CI uses a sampled ephemeral key which is documented in the workflow."
Ethan: "Add a smoke test to avoid flakes."
Priya: "Added queue unit test and deterministic harness — CI green locally and in actions."

Backward compatibility and safety: This quickstart contains no runtime or SDK changes to production code paths; it is purely an examples/doc addition. No breaking changes. Adapters follow the public tool-binding guidance and include a mapping table to make migrations straightforward.

Documentation highlights: The README includes a short section mapping the sample orchestrator primitives to Redwood runtime features: batching, KV-cache mock behavior, fallback routing, and example rollout settings. The quickstart demonstrates how to tether a local index and run a simulated user session while capturing span traces and probe metrics (opt-out).

How to try locally: follow quickstart.md: clone repo, open in devcontainer, yarn install and yarn run smoke. Quickstart boots an example index (in-memory), spins up the orchestrator, issues a simulated query and demonstrates a plugin call and a fallback to cached embeddings.

Related work: ENG-4813 (authoring quickstarts sprint) and PM-998 (improve onboarding for tool-calling RAG flows).

Merge: After addressing reviewer feedback and stabilizing CI the PR was merged via squash on 2024-12-03.
notes: This quickstart is intentionally compact: the orchestrator focuses on authoring patterns and test harnesses rather than production runtime optimizations. It is intended as a teaching and onboarding artifact.
notes_long: Design decisions: 1) Keep the orchestrator <= 250 lines to encourage reading end-to-end; 2) Provide both in-process and HTTP adapter shims so engineers can prototype local tools quickly; 3) Opt-out telemetry so quickstarts remain privacy-friendly while allowing Redwood to collect sampled telemetry for CI health checks when enabled. Future: add a Python variant and a short video walkthrough.
